clue.text: Clever person from UK about to fix line back

indicators.note: the word for a Briton goes around the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: a Brit is a native of Britain

indicators.note: the words for fixing and line are read from the end to the start

parts.note: to nail something is to fix it in place

explanation.surface: A smart Briton seems to be mending a cable or fishing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the fixing word plus L, making LLIAN, and 'about' wraps the Briton round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone exceptionally intelligent or talented; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Audacious dance event supporting Bishop

indicators.note: in a down clue the dance word sits underneath, holding up the bishop's letter

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a rave is a large all-night dance party

explanation.surface: A daring dance party is held in support of a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Audacious and the answer are synonyms for showing courage or daring.

clue.text: Without saying too much, it's provided to carry brine at sea

indicators.note: the condition word holds the other letters inside it, as if carrying them

parts.note: provided, as in on condition that, means if

indicators.note: being all at sea means confused, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A ship's tanks seem able to hold salt water while sailing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' scrambles the salt water into NBRIE, which 'to carry' places inside the condition word; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning briefly or concisely, saying little.

clue.text: Chalky material recalled found in Marsanne (not Semillon)

indicators.note: called back, so the run of letters is read from right to left
the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A wine note: Marsanne, not Semillon, gives a chalky mineral character.
explanation.walkthrough: Marsanne and Semillon are both white wine grapes; the wine-tasting picture hides the reversed run spanning the end of Marsanne, all of 'not' and the start of Semillon.
explanation.definitionFit: This sedimentary rock, of which chalk is a soft form, is a chalky material.

clue.text: Articles about American trial broadcast from Sydney?

indicators.note: the two articles go round the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a and an are the indefinite articles
an is the other indefinite article
US is short for American, as in United States

indicators.note: scattered widely, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A news item about an American court case being transmitted from Sydney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' makes TRALI. The question mark flags that Sydney is just one example of an Antipodean city.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something from Sydney is from the country down under, so this is definition by example.

clue.text: Roman official missing ridicule in song

indicators.note: the official's title lacks the letters of the teasing word

parts.note: a tribune was an elected official in ancient Rome
to rib someone is to tease or ridicule them

explanation.surface: A Roman magistrate, without mockery, breaks into song.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune is a melody, which is what a song is sung to; near synonyms.

clue.text: Fellow, university visitor, forgetting street in form of amnesia

indicators.note: the visitor's word leaves out the street's letters, as if they slipped the mind

parts.note: a guest is a visitor

explanation.surface: A university fellow forgets which street a visitor came from: a bout of amnesia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgetting' is apt: the clue's own picture is forgetfulness.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissociative fugue is a psychiatric state of memory loss, often with unplanned travel.

clue.text: Manage to catch luminance in distress signal

indicators.note: the word for managing holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: to fare is to get on or manage, as in how did you fare
L is the physics symbol for luminance

explanation.surface: Trying to pick up light from a distress signal at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A flare is a bright pyrotechnic fired to summon rescue, a standard emergency signal.

clue.text: Instruments, black in form, mostly

indicators.note: the tar letters go inside the shortened word for form
most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: guise means outward form or appearance
tar is black, and is a crossword stand-in for it

explanation.surface: Instruments finished mostly in black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the form word, leaving GUIS, and 'in' puts the black stuff inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: These are stringed instruments, examples of the general class named.

clue.text: Persuasive words showing merry Queen Cole

indicators.note: the nursery-rhyme adjective doubles as a sign that the letters are tipsily rearranged

explanation.surface: Echoes Old King Cole, the merry old soul, now as a queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Old King Cole is a nursery-rhyme monarch described as 'a merry old soul'.
explanation.definitionFit: Persuasive, fluent speech or writing is what this word for expressive power means.

clue.text: Almost completely useless recording

indicators.note: nearly all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: all means completely, as in all alone
bum is slang for worthless or useless, as in a bum deal

explanation.surface: A judgment that a record is pretty much a total dud.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a collection of tracks issued as one record, a type of recording.

clue.text: Country resettling Romanians

indicators.note: people settling in a new place suggests the letters moving into new positions

explanation.surface: A nation where Romanian migrants are making new homes.
explanation.definitionFit: This microstate enclaved within Italy is a sovereign country.

clue.text: Messenger to fail, coming in before time without first of letters

indicators.note: the word for failing enters the shortened word for being ahead of time
the word loses the initial letter of the clue word that follows

parts.note: early means before the expected time

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: to miss is to fail to hit or achieve

explanation.surface: A messenger fails to arrive early and the letters never get through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of letters' is L; 'without' removes it from the before-time word, leaving EARY, and 'coming in' places the failing word inside after its E.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy sent with a message or mission is a messenger, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Memory disorder unfortunately due to limit a lot of web language

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit at either side, bounding the others
things going badly suggests letters knocked out of order
most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: Java is a programming language widely used on the web

explanation.surface: A programmer's complaint that the deadline caps how much code they can write.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' makes DEU; 'a lot of' trims the language to JAV, and 'to limit' sets it after DE.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase names the uncanny illusion of having already lived the present moment, a memory glitch.

clue.text: Second year — year defined by interaction of sun and moon — having same meaning

indicators.note: defined in the sense of bounded, so the year's letter is enclosed
the two words act on one another, mixing their letters

parts.note: Y again stands for year

explanation.surface: An astronomy note: a year is defined by how the sun and moon move together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interaction of' mixes the two bodies into NONMOUS, and 'defined by' (bounded by) sets the second year's Y inside after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Words with the same meaning are synonyms; this adjective describes such words.

clue.text: Gold and iron ring featuring in opera

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Gold and iron jewellery appears in an opera, perhaps Wagner's Ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Monteverdi's and Gluck's operas on the Orpheus myth both carry this Italian title.

clue.text: Religious graduate taking Biblical book into Arab state for general worker

indicators.note: the graduate and book go inside the state's name

parts.note: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian peninsula
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a degree in theology
Job is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A divinity doctor carries a Bible book into Oman for a labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who does assorted small tasks is a handyman, a general worker.

clue.text: Supplies will accommodate a non-professional

indicators.note: the supplying phrase takes the other letters in, housing them

parts.note: lays on means supplies or provides, as in lays on food
per means a, as in once per day

explanation.surface: Provisions will house an amateur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a' is not an article here but 'per', as in so much a day.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without specialist training in a field is an amateur, not a professional.

clue.text: Arrangement of Eroica set to offer strange stuff

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reworks a piece, here reordering the letters

explanation.surface: A new arrangement of Beethoven's Eroica symphony offers something odd.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eroica is Beethoven's Third Symphony; 'Arrangement' fits the musical picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure, arcane items known to few are odd or recondite things, strange stuff.

clue.text: Outlaw in business pursuing game animals, bagging little special

indicators.note: the business word follows after the rest
the animals' word takes the abbreviation inside, as a hunter bags game

parts.note: deer are hunted as game
SP is a short form of special; little signals the abbreviation
ado means fuss or business, as in much ado

explanation.surface: An outlaw hunting deer in some special operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless criminal of the Wild West, an outlaw.

clue.text: A million in Essex unexpectedly like gay marriage

indicators.note: the article and million letter sit inside the jumbled county
turned out differently than expected, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A million weddings in Essex, unexpectedly of the same-sex kind.
explanation.walkthrough: Essex is an English county east of London. 'unexpectedly' makes ESSEX into SESEX; 'in' puts AM after its first S.
explanation.definitionFit: Marriage between two men or two women is between partners of one gender.

clue.text: Limits to one accepting cigarette, though old enough

indicators.note: the outer letters take the cigarette word between them
only the boundary letters, the first and last, are used

parts.note: fag is British slang for a cigarette

explanation.surface: Someone taking a cigarette though they are now legally old enough.
explanation.walkthrough: FAG is everyday British slang for a cigarette. 'Limits to one' gives O and E, which 'accepting' wraps around FAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of legal adult age means being old enough, an idiom for the law's threshold.

clue.text: Foolish son entering excellent square

indicators.note: the son's letter goes inside the word for excellent

parts.note: A1, written AI, means first-class or excellent
nine is a square number, three times three

explanation.surface: A foolish son walks into a fine town square.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means top quality; the digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means extremely silly or senseless, a synonym of foolish.

clue.text: Enthusiasm to capture a brass sound

indicators.note: the enthusiasm word holds the article inside it

parts.note: oomph means energy or zest

explanation.surface: Zeal needed to record the noise of a brass band.
explanation.definitionFit: The word imitates the deep rhythmic notes of a tuba or brass band.

clue.text: Money included in nineteen letters? Very small amounts

indicators.note: the money letter is placed inside the alphabet span

parts.note: the alphabet from A to S covers nineteen letters, so A TO S

explanation.surface: Cash enclosed in nineteen pieces of post amounts to very little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nineteen letters?' is A TO S, the first nineteen letters of the alphabet; the question mark flags that wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiniest particles of matter stand figuratively for minute quantities, as in not an iota.

clue.text: Promotional material — run charged item identifying godlike entity

parts.note: hype is extravagant publicity
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
an ion is an electrically charged atom or molecule

explanation.surface: Publicity runs a charged story identifying a god-like figure.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this is a Titan, one of the divine race preceding the Olympians.

clue.text: Government blocking insubstantial uprising at the end of the day

indicators.note: the government letter sits inside, blocking the reversed word
in a down clue the word rises, so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: thin means flimsy or insubstantial

explanation.surface: A government suppressing a feeble revolt, when all is said and done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns THIN into NIHT; 'blocking' puts G inside. 'at the end of the day' looks like a filler idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark hours follow evening, so it comes at the close of the day.

clue.text: Power and skill in what musician plays

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics
art means skill, as in the art of persuasion

explanation.surface: Strength and technique are what a performer brings to the music.
explanation.definitionFit: In an ensemble each player performs their own line of the score, a part.

clue.text: Company against promotional material musician's brought round — sweet stuff

indicators.note: the musician word goes round the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: muso is informal British slang for a musician; the 's is 'has'
V is short for versus, meaning against
an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: A firm opposed to advertising that a musician has circulated, over sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: This dark, moist unrefined cane sugar is literally a sweet substance.

clue.text: Decorative stuff hard to miss in approach to divination

indicators.note: the hard letter is omitted from the divination word

parts.note: the I Ching is an ancient Chinese system of divination
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Fortune-telling without effort is a decorative extra.
explanation.definitionFit: The sugary coating on a cake is ornamental, the stuff that decorates it.

clue.text: Invader of England switching directions for Greek island

indicators.note: the two compass letters change places, each taking the other's spot
the compass points north and south are the letters swapped here

parts.note: the Saxons invaded England after the Romans left

explanation.surface: An invader of England heads off in a new direction to a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switching directions' swaps the S (south) and N (north) in SAXON.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the largest of the Cyclades in the Aegean, a Greek island.

clue.text: Witness quiet number entering examination

indicators.note: the quiet and number letters go inside the examination word

parts.note: a test is an examination
tame means docile or quiet

explanation.surface: A witness is quietly numbered among those taking the exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament is evidence or proof, as in bearing witness to something.
